controls.title: Mind map
controls.summary: A tree of ideas laid out automatically from a root, with edges drawn by the control.
controls.when: Brainstorming, outlines, plans, taxonomies, org charts (direction down) — any hierarchy a reader takes in at a glance.
controls.agent:
# mindmap — a mind map control

A `buckyos.container` with `kind: "mindmap"` on a canvas (a Surface or a group). Its nodes are ordinary Blocks
(`buckyos.cell`): `parent_id` is the tree (a node's children sit under it), `order_key` the sibling order. The
control lays the nodes out and draws the edges between parent and child; nothing about edges is stored.

## Rules

- **Do not compute coordinates.** Give every node `placement: { "x": "auto", "y": "auto", "w": "auto", "h": "auto" }`
  (or no placement at all). The control's `tree` layout places them; a number in a component pins it.
- The control itself: `placement: { x, y, w: "auto", h: "auto" }` with numbers for x / y (its first root's
  top-left on the canvas; omit placement on a flow page). Its `layout` is `{ "mode": "tree" }` (implied).
- Text nodes: `view: { type: "mindnode" }`, the text in `title` (at most 256 characters; inline Markdown —
  **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [links](https://…) — is kept and shown formatted).
- A node may be any Block (an image, a table view, a shape…). A node that is not a text view (mindnode, shape,
  richtext) needs numeric `w` / `h`: `{ "x": "auto", "y": "auto", "w": 240, "h": 160 }`.
- A node may itself be another mindmap control (its own tree inside one node).
- Normally one root node directly under the container; several roots are stacked.
- Relation lines between nodes are ordinary connectors on the canvas (`view.type: connector`), not children.
- Folding is each reader's own view state: you always see (and write) the whole tree.

## Config (`payload.config`, all optional)

| key | values | default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | `right` · `left` · `both` (root in the middle) · `down` (org chart) | `right` |
| `edge` | `curve` · `elbow` · `straight` | `curve` |
| `spacing` | `{ sibling, level }` in px (0–2000) | `{ sibling: 12, level: 48 }` |
| `branch_colors` | up to 64 `#rrggbb` colours for the first-level branches | a built-in palette |

A node's `config` may carry `branch_color` (`#rrggbb`, inherited by its subtree) and, on a first-level node of a
`both` map, `side: "left" | "right"`.

## Create one with doc.commit

```json
[
  { "op": "entity.create", "entity_id": "mm1", "type_id": "buckyos.container", "parent_id": "<surface id>", "order_key": "m",
    "placement": { "x": 100, "y": 100, "w": "auto", "h": "auto" },
    "payload": { "kind": "mindmap", "title": "Launch plan", "config": { "direction": "both" } } },
  { "op": "entity.create", "entity_id": "mm1-root", "type_id": "buckyos.cell", "parent_id": "mm1", "order_key": "a",
    "placement": { "x": "auto", "y": "auto", "w": "auto", "h": "auto" },
    "payload": { "view": { "type": "mindnode" }, "title": "Launch plan" } },
  { "op": "entity.create", "entity_id": "mm1-a", "type_id": "buckyos.cell", "parent_id": "mm1-root", "order_key": "a",
    "placement": { "x": "auto", "y": "auto", "w": "auto", "h": "auto" },
    "payload": { "view": { "type": "mindnode" }, "title": "Market" } },
  { "op": "entity.create", "entity_id": "mm1-a1", "type_id": "buckyos.cell", "parent_id": "mm1-a", "order_key": "a",
    "placement": { "x": "auto", "y": "auto", "w": "auto", "h": "auto" },
    "payload": { "view": { "type": "mindnode" }, "title": "**User** interviews" } }
]
```

Add a branch later: `entity.create` Cells under an existing node (`parent_id` = that node, an `order_key` after its
last child). Move a branch: `tree.move` the node to another node, placement stays `"auto"`. Delete a branch:
`entity.delete` the node with `subtree: { delete: [every descendant id] }`.

## Exchange formats

- **Markdown outline** (preferred): a nested list, optionally under headings; one top-level item is the root.
  `buckyos aiws import <file.md> --workspace <ws> --parent <surface id> [--at x,y]` creates the map;
  `buckyos aiws export <control id> --workspace <ws> [--format opml]` reads it back. In a wish:
  `aiws.result.control(name, { kind: "mindmap", children: "<markdown outline>" })`; to grow a node that is an
  input, add `under: "<input name>"` (its current branch reads as an outline).
- **OPML**: the same tree as `<outline text>` elements (`--format opml`, or an `.opml` file to import).

## Don'ts

- No numbers for node x / y / w / h unless you mean to pin a node (and a non-text node's size).
- No connectors inside the control, no data entities under it, no `layout` other than `{ mode: tree }`.
- Nodes stay inside their control: to put a branch elsewhere, create a copy there and delete the original.

controls.title: Composite control
controls.summary: The host of every composite extension control: a container whose definition (def_ref) lays out the Blocks of its slots and draws a frame around them.
controls.when: To place an instance of a composite control a Workspace defines (data/extensions, kind composite); as a wish result it is a control result naming the definition (def) and filling its slots, never this kind.
controls.agent:
# Composite controls A composite instance is `buckyos.container { kind: "composite", def_ref: { entity_id: }, config?, bindings?, layout: { mode: "def" } }`. Its definition (a `buckyos.block-def` with `kind: "composite"`) carries `composition { layout, slots, chrome }` and an AGENT.md self-description: read it first (`doc.read` the definition). Every child of the instance is an ordinary Block with `slot` set to a slot of the composition; several Blocks may fill one slot (the definition's `max` and `accepts` say how many and what). Placement: in a `stack` layout write `{ x: "auto", y: "auto", w, h }` on the children and `{ x, y, w: "auto", h: "auto" }` on the instance — the host computes the rest; a `fixed` layout needs numeric x / y. Never compute coordinates the control computes. Example (doc.commit): `{ op: "entity.create", entity_id: "b1", type_id: "buckyos.container", parent_id: , order_key: "m", placement: { x: 40, y: 40, w: "auto", h: "auto" }, payload: { kind: "composite", def_ref: { entity_id: }, config: { title: "Today" } } }`, then `{ op: "entity.create", entity_id: "c1", type_id: "buckyos.cell", parent_id: "b1", order_key: "a", placement: { x: "auto", y: "auto", w: 240, h: 120 }, payload: { view: { type: "html" }, def_ref: { entity_id: }, slot: "cards" } }`. Copy an instance with `tree.clone` (its children and own data come along, the definition is shared). Moving a Block in or out: `tree.move` with `slot`. `layout.algorithm` `grid` (columns, gap) fills cells row by row: children get `{ x: "auto", y: "auto", w, h }` as in a stack. Events: the definition's `events` (outline `def_events`) re-raise events of the slots' controls (`from: { slot, event }`). An instance binds handlers in `on: { : handler | [handlers] }` — `{ kind: "write", target: , what: recordSet | upsert | setMarkdown, args }`, `{ kind: "wish", wish_id }`, `{ kind: "open", target? }`, `{ kind: "notify", text }`, strings with `{{event.

}}` / `{{config.}}`; they run when a person clicks in run mode. Change `config` / `bindings` / `on` one property at a time with `entity.set_props`. As a wish result: `aiws.result.control(name, { def: "#", config?, slots: { : ["result:" | "input:" | { view: "richtext", markdown }] }, under?: { input, slot } })` — the other results' Blocks, copies of input Blocks and new texts fill the slots.

controls.title: To-do
controls.summary: A to-do list that is also a board: the records of a to-do table, ticked, reordered and moved between status columns.
controls.when: To show and work through a to-do table (buckyos.todo@1) on a canvas: a checklist, a task board.
controls.agent:
# todo — the to-do control (list and board)

A `buckyos.container` with `kind: "todo"` on a canvas. It shows one to-do table (a `buckyos.table-source` with
`schema_id: "buckyos.todo@1"`) bound as `bindings.items`. **The items are the table's records**: to add, complete,
move or rename a to-do, write the table (`table.insert_records` / `table.set_values`), never Blocks — the control
shows the change at once. Nothing is stored per item in the control.

## The table (fields by id)

| field | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | text, required | the to-do |
| `status` | select, required | a column of the board, in option order; option `done` means completed (default options `todo`, `doing`, `done`) |
| `due` | date | due date |
| `order` | text | an order key (base-36 fractional index, as `order_key`): list and column order |
| `done_at` | datetime | when it was completed |
| `ext` | json object | `priority` (low / normal / high / urgent), `tags` (strings), `assignee`, `reminders` |

A record's body (`table.set_body`, a rich text under the table) holds its notes.

## The control

`payload: { kind: "todo", layout: { mode: "data" }, title?, bindings: { items: { entity_id: <table> } }, config? }` with a
numeric `placement { x, y, w, h }` (it holds no Blocks). `config` is the default view: `mode` (`list` | `board`),
`hide_done` (boolean), `collapsed` (status option ids of folded columns). Each person's own view is their user state.

## Create one with doc.commit

```json
{ "op": "entity.create", "entity_id": "todo1", "type_id": "buckyos.table-source", "schema_id": "buckyos.todo@1", "parent_id": "<content folder>",
  "order_key": "a", "payload": { "title_field_id": "title", "fields": [
    { "field_id": "title", "name": "Title", "type": "text", "required": true },
    { "field_id": "status", "name": "Status", "type": "select", "required": true, "options": [{ "option_id": "todo", "label": "To do" }, { "option_id": "doing", "label": "In progress" }, { "option_id": "done", "label": "Done" }] },
    { "field_id": "due", "name": "Due", "type": "date", "nullable": true }, { "field_id": "order", "name": "Order", "type": "text", "nullable": true },
    { "field_id": "done_at", "name": "Completed", "type": "datetime", "nullable": true }, { "field_id": "ext", "name": "Extension", "type": "json", "nullable": true }] } }
{ "op": "entity.create", "entity_id": "todoctl1", "type_id": "buckyos.container", "parent_id": "<surface>", "order_key": "b",
  "placement": { "x": 40, "y": 40, "w": 420, "h": 560 }, "payload": { "kind": "todo", "layout": { "mode": "data" }, "bindings": { "items": { "entity_id": "todo1" } } } }
{ "op": "table.insert_records", "source_id": "todo1", "records": [{ "record_id": "t1", "values": { "title": "Buy milk", "status": "todo", "order": "i" } }] }
```

The placement is numbers (never `"auto"`): a data control is sized like a Block.

## The private schedule

Every person has a Workspace named `schedule` (`ws.ensure { name: "schedule" }`) whose to-do table has the fixed id
`todo` (and calendar `calendar`). Use the `buckyos aiws todo` commands (or buckyos-websdk `ScheduleClient`) to
read and change it.

controls.title: Calendar
controls.summary: A day / week / month / agenda calendar of the events in calendar tables, repeating events included.
controls.when: To show and edit events of a calendar table (buckyos.calendar@1) on a canvas: meetings, plans, a team calendar.
controls.agent:
# calendar — the calendar control

A `buckyos.container` with `kind: "calendar"`. It shows the calendar tables (`schema_id: "buckyos.calendar@1"`) listed
in `bindings.events` and the due dates of the to-do tables (`buckyos.todo@1`, read only) listed in `bindings.todo`:
both bindings are lists, `[{ "entity_id": … }, …]`. **Events are the table's records**: write the table, never Blocks.

## The table (fields by id)

| field | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | text, required | |
| `all_day` | boolean | an all-day event (absent: timed) |
| `start` / `end` | datetime (RFC 3339) | a timed event; `end` not before `start` |
| `start_date` / `end_date` | date | an all-day event, `end_date` inclusive |
| `status` | select | confirmed / tentative / cancelled |
| `ext` | json object | `rrule` (iCalendar RRULE subset), `exdate` (excluded original starts), `recurrence_id` `{ master, original }` (overrides one occurrence), `tz` (IANA zone the series repeats in), `location`, `color`, `reminders`, `rule_text` + `occurrences` + `covered_until` (rules outside the subset, occurrences an Agent wrote), `maintenance` |

Repeating: `FREQ=DAILY|WEEKLY|MONTHLY|YEARLY`, `INTERVAL`, `COUNT` or `UNTIL`, `BYDAY` (ordinals with monthly /
yearly: `-1FR` = last Friday), `BYMONTHDAY`, `BYMONTH`, `BYSETPOS`, `WKST`. Every weekday:
`FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR`. An occurrence's id is `<record_id>@<original start>`. "Only this one" writes an
override record; "skip today" adds the original to `ext.exdate`.

## The control

`payload: { kind: "calendar", layout: { mode: "data" }, title?, bindings: { events: [{ entity_id }, …], todo?: [{ entity_id }, …] }, config? }`
with a numeric placement. `config`: `view` (`day` | `week` | `month` | `agenda`), `week_start` (0 Monday … 6 Sunday),
`day_start` (first hour shown), `colors` (`{ <table entity id>: "#rrggbb" }`; otherwise each table gets the next colour).

## Create one with doc.commit

```json
{ "op": "entity.create", "entity_id": "calctl1", "type_id": "buckyos.container", "parent_id": "<surface>", "order_key": "c",
  "placement": { "x": 40, "y": 40, "w": 880, "h": 640 }, "payload": { "kind": "calendar", "layout": { "mode": "data" }, "bindings": { "events": [{ "entity_id": "<calendar table>" }] }, "config": { "view": "week" } } }
{ "op": "table.insert_records", "source_id": "<calendar table>", "records": [
  { "record_id": "e1", "values": { "title": "Stand-up", "start": "2026-11-16T01:00:00Z", "end": "2026-11-16T01:15:00Z", "ext": { "rrule": "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR", "tz": "Asia/Shanghai" } } },
  { "record_id": "e2", "values": { "title": "Trip", "all_day": true, "start_date": "2026-11-20", "end_date": "2026-11-22" } }] }
```

The placement is numbers (never `"auto"`): a data control is sized like a Block.

Use `buckyos aiws cal` (or buckyos-websdk `ScheduleClient`) to read and change the private schedule.
